blocks.text: King George Corridor home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

123 condos sold in King George Corridor with a median price of $553,000 (the middle half sold between $497,500 and $610,250), taking a median of 29 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 2% sold above list. They had a median $542 per square foot, a median year built of 2004 and a median strata fee of $500 a month. 77 townhomes sold in King George Corridor with a median price of $776,000 (the middle half sold between $730,000 and $888,000), taking a median of 25 days to sell at 96.9% of the last list price; 1% sold above list. They had a median $499 per square foot, a median year built of 2008 and a median strata fee of $431 a month.

items.t: The City of Surrey's King George Corridor plan area runs along King George Boulevard from 8 Avenue in the south to the Nicomekl River in the north, with Highway 99 at the east — roughly 7 km and about 490 hectares (1,210 acres). It began as a 1995 concept plan; its designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update (current OCP: Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026), carried through Corporate Report R246, endorsed December 2, 2024. The City page states no named west boundary road, so the west edge is UNVERIFIED beyond the plan map itself.

The south end of the corridor overlaps the Semiahmoo Town Centre Plan area (roughly 16 to 24 Avenues), which is why the newest buildings cluster around 17 Avenue and 152 Street. One listing feed card for this sub-area carried a White Rock civic address — the sub-area straddles the Surrey–White Rock line at its south end, and whether a specific unit is in Surrey or White Rock is an address-level check.

Transit on the corridor today is bus: the live page names routes 321 (King George Boulevard) and 345, with frequencies UNVERIFIED in this research. The planned King George Boulevard BRT would run about 19 km with 12 stations from Surrey City Centre to Semiahmoo Town Centre on dedicated lanes, every 5 minutes at peak, about 40 minutes end to end (roughly 40% faster than the current trip); Surrey Council has moved it to full design. Only the BRT's south portion crosses this plan area — the rest of the route is Whalley and Newton ground.

The corridor's north edge is a river, not a road: the Nicomekl River bounds the plan area, Surrey's coastal floodplain mapping covers the Nicomekl/Serpentine lowlands, and the City is building Nicomekl Riverfront Park on the river's south bank. Flood construction levels are set parcel by parcel, so the flood status of any specific building site is UNVERIFIED without a parcel-level check.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in King George Corridor

items.t: The Form B Information Certificate is the buyer's core document in every corridor strata: under s. 59 of the Strata Property Act the strata must provide it within 7 days of a request, for a fee of no more than $35 plus up to 25 cents per page for copies. In this corridor it does double duty — it is the only document that proves whether the 55+ and no-pets descriptions attached to Suncliff Place and The Cambridge are registered bylaws or just listing copy.
Minimum CRF contribution: since November 1, 2023, stratas must contribute at least 10% of the annual operating fund to the contingency reserve fund each year.

Rentals: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 — any older directory or disclosure line in this corridor restricting rentals no longer has legal effect, though a strata may still ban or regulate short-term rentals.

Age bylaws: the only age-restriction bylaw a BC strata may enforce is 55+, under ss. 123.1 and 123.2 of the Strata Property Act, with exemptions added May 1, 2023 (caregivers, and spouses/partners who met the requirement when they moved in, among them). Listings describe both Suncliff Place and The Cambridge as 55+; a 19+ or any other age line in an old document would be void, and the 55+ claim itself stands or falls on the registered bylaws.
Pets: pet limits and bans remain lawful strata bylaws.

Zoning: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 governs the corridor, and the plan framework above it is now the Surrey 2050 OCP (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026) — the 1995 corridor concept plan's designations were superseded through Corporate Report R246 (endorsed December 2, 2024), so an old disclosure citing the 1995 plan is citing history, not current zoning.

Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH): Surrey permits 3 units on lots under 280 m² and 4 units on lots over 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of 281 m² or more within 400 m of a frequent bus stop — King George Boulevard's bus service makes that frequent-stop band relevant to the corridor's remaining house lots, though not to its strata complexes. One secondary suite per house is permitted under the BC Building Code framework; an unpermitted suite is not made legal by the SSMUH rules.

Floodplain: the corridor's north end sits in the Nicomekl lowlands. Surrey's flood control pages cover the Serpentine–Nicomekl lowlands, and flood construction levels are parcel-specific — a buyer near the river end should confirm the building's flood construction level rather than rely on the sub-area map.

Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty applied after July 2 and a further 5% after September 2. South-end addresses near the White Rock line need the municipality checked — a White Rock civic address pays White Rock taxes on White Rock's schedule, not Surrey's.

GST on new builds is 5% — it applies to developer sales (relevant to remaining developer inventory at 2025 completions like King + Crescent and Halvo) and not to ordinary resales. The first-time home buyers' GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026, per CRA Excise and GST/HST News No. 122) rebates 100% of the GST on a new home priced up to $1M (maximum $50,000), phasing out to $1.5M, for agreements entered into from March 20, 2025 to 2031. The older GST New Housing Rebate covers homes the FTHB rebate does not: 36% of the GST, maximum $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000.

BC Property Transfer Tax: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% on the portion up to $2M, 3% above $2M, plus a further 2% on the residential portion of a price above $3M. The First-Time Home Buyers' exemption is full up to $835,000 fair market value (on the first $500,000) and partial up to $860,000; the Newly Built Home Exemption is full up to $1.1M and partial up to $1.15M.

Federal first-time buyer tools: the Home Buyers' Plan allows a $60,000 RRSP withdrawal; the First Home Savings Account allows $40,000 lifetime at $8,000 per year. CMHC mortgage insurance premiums run 0.6%–4.5%.

Presales: REDMA gives a 7-day rescission period under s. 21 and requires purchase deposits to be held in trust under s. 18 — the framework for any assignment or remaining developer contract in the corridor's new buildings.

blocks.text: Good to know about King George Corridor

items.t: Two of the corridor's "buildings" are secretly pairs with different ages: Stratford Gardens carries 1995 and 1996 build years across its two addresses, and Ocean Bay Villas carries 2003 and 2004 across its three — a unit's building age follows its own address, not the complex name.

The Cambridge name is also a pair, not a building: The Cambridge (15270 17 Avenue, 1985, described as 55+) and Cambridge II (15300 17 Avenue, 1987 or 1988 — listings conflict) are separate stratas a block apart, and a search under one name will surface the other's listings.

The corridor's plan is older than most of its buildings and no longer the law: the 1995 concept plan's designations were superseded when the Surrey 2050 OCP update was carried through Corporate Report R246 in December 2024, so marketing that quotes the 1995 plan is quoting a repealed framework.

The sub-area straddles a municipal border: at least one listing in this sub-area's own feed carried a White Rock civic address, which changes the tax authority, the tax due dates and the school district side of the line — the postal address, not the sub-area label, decides.

Peace Arch Hospital in White Rock is the hospital serving this corridor, and the day-to-day retail anchor is Semiahmoo Town Centre at the 16–24 Avenue end — the corridor's newest buildings (Halvo, the Cambridge pair) sit within that town-centre orbit, not out on the boulevard itself.

Recreation is split between two facilities buyers often conflate: the South Surrey Recreation & Arts Centre at 14601 20 Avenue and the larger Grandview Heights Aquatic Centre at 16855 24 Avenue, with Semiahmoo Library at 1815 152 Street and Ocean Park Library at 12854 17 Avenue serving the corridor's ends.
The condo side of this road is the liquid side.

The City page as read states no named west boundary road — UNVERIFIED as a named road. The corridor's 1995 concept-plan designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update, following Council's December 2, 2024 endorsement of Corporate Report R246. Municipality and community: City of Surrey, in the City-published community of South Surrey; one feed card carried a White Rock civic address under the same sub-area label — the sub-area straddles the Surrey–White Rock boundary at its south end, so the municipality of a specific unit is an address-level check.

Parent community (S Surrey White Rock) medians — sub-area medians are not published: UNVERIFIED at sub-area level: detached $1,628,000; attached $700,000, $524/sq ft, 99% sale-to-list, 33 days on market.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: the two counted complexes stand at the corridor's Semiahmoo end — Keystone fronting the boulevard itself at 2925 King George Boulevard, and Peninsula Village on 152 Street at 2500 152 Street, beside the Peninsula Village Shopping Centre. The corridor's apartment stock (not townhomes) clusters around 17 Avenue / 152 Street and 146A Street.

SD36 catchments are address-based and no locator run for a King George Corridor address is on record — the one South Surrey locator result on record (1785 148 St → H. T. Thrift Elementary / Semiahmoo Secondary) is for a Sunnyside Park address, not a corridor address, and is NOT reused here — so the catchment school for any specific corridor address is UNVERIFIED.

Transit today is bus: the live page names routes 321 (Surrey Central Station to White Rock Centre via King George Boulevard) and 345 (King George Station to White Rock Centre); frequencies and span are UNVERIFIED in the research. Transit planned: TransLink is advancing King George Boulevard BRT — approximately 19 km with 12 stations connecting Surrey City Centre and Semiahmoo Town Centre, dedicated lanes, transit signal priority, peak service every five minutes, and end-to-end peak travel times reduced by approximately 40% to about 40 minutes; the City states Council voted to move the project into the full design stage.

Floodplain at the north end: the corridor's north edge is the Nicomekl River, and Surrey's coastal floodplain runs along the Nicomekl and Serpentine Rivers and the Serpentine–Nicomekl lowlands; the City is building Nicomekl Riverfront Park along the river's south bank at the corridor's north end. Parcel-level flood levels: UNVERIFIED — confirmed with the City per parcel.

Health and recreation: Peace Arch Hospital in White Rock serves the South Surrey / White Rock area. The South Surrey Recreation & Arts Centre (14601 20 Avenue), Grandview Heights Aquatic Centre (16855 24 Avenue) and the Semiahmoo (1815 152 Street) and Ocean Park (12854 17 Avenue) library branches serve corridor residents.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in King George Corridor

items.t: Form B diligence (both counted strata complexes): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For Peninsula Village the Form B is also where the published 55+ position is actually proved — listing statements are not proof.

blocks.text: Good to know about King George Corridor

items.t: The name is the trap: one road, two markets. "King George Corridor" on this page, in the City plan and in the board data means 8 Avenue to the Nicomekl River only.

South Surrey's best-known 55+ townhouse complex and its nearest 55+ neighbour are in different MLS sub-areas. Peninsula Village (2500 152 St, King George Corridor filing) and Bishop's Green (2533 152 St, Sunnyside Park filing) stand a few blocks apart on the same street, both gated 55+-described townhouse complexes — a buyer searching only one sub-area's page misses the other.
One listing also calls Peninsula Village "The Peninsula." Same address (2500 152 St), same strata plan (LMS 133), two marketing names — an alert set on one name does not cover the other.

Keystone's own listings argue about which sub-area it is in. One current listing records Subdivision: King George Corridor; others record Elgin Chantrell for the same 2925 King George Boulevard address.

The sub-area straddles a municipal border. At least one listing in this sub-area's own feed carried a White Rock civic address, which changes the tax authority, the tax due dates and the school district side of the line — the postal address, not the sub-area label, decides.
The attached side of this road is the liquid side. Within that attached depth, the named townhouse stock is just two complexes; the rest of the liquidity is apartment condos.

The LMS 133 report a search surfaces first (JRS Engineering, October 15, 2014) predates the current five-year cycle — a buyer should ask for the most recent report in the Form B package, not price the complex off the 2014 document.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in King George Corridor?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 131 condos and townhomes listed in King George Corridor. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is King George Corridor a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in King George Corridor had a sales ratio of 21%, which the reports’ scale reads as a sellers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in King George Corridor from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 89 condos and townhomes sold in King George Corridor over those 4 months, out of 375 in all of South Surrey and White Rock.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did condos in King George Corridor sell for?
faq.a: 123 condos sold in King George Corridor between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $553,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in King George Corridor?
faq.a: The median was 29 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.1% of the last list price (2% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Is this the same King George corridor as the SkyTrain towers downtown?
faq.a: No. The towers around King George Station are in Whalley, on the same road's north end, and are documented in the city-wide Surrey files. This corridor is the low-rise South Surrey segment from 8 Avenue to the Nicomekl River, and Surrey City Centre land is Whalley board ground.

faq.q: Keystone fronts the boulevard like an apartment block — is it condos or townhouses?
faq.a: Townhouses. Listings classify its units Row / Townhouse, 3 storeys, built 2011, and built form governs over the streetscape impression.

faq.q: Is Peninsula Village really 55+ — and do both of us have to be 55?
faq.a: Listings state the rule as "One person 55+," and 55+ is the one age bylaw BC law permits — but a listing statement is not proof; the registered bylaw on the Form B is. Provincially, a younger spouse or partner of a resident who meets the age requirement (or holds a legacy exemption) is exempt, as are live-in caregivers and legacy residents (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, Reg 7.01 as expanded May 1, 2023).

faq.q: Can I rent out my corridor townhouse?
faq.a: Long-term, yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022, whatever an older document prints.

faq.q: What about the townhouse-classified units inside King + Crescent?
faq.a: Ask for the King + Crescent Form B package in the condos frame.
